Exit 0 means the misuse was silently accepted\". The diff changes that exit to 3 and redefines the contract in prose only. Nothing in this repository implements either contract: `check.sh --full` runs `zig build examples`, which only COMPILES both cq examples, and the single example harness it does carry is the `stderr-smoke` block (check.sh:153-176). `.github/workflows/test.yml` calls only `check.sh`. So the new rule is unenforced here, and any out-of-tree checker still applying the old, previously documented rule now reads exit 3 as \"non-zero, therefore the panic fired\" — a pass. The failure mode this example exists to catch (two drivers silently accepted) becomes invisible, and it fails open rather than loud. Second, weaker point at the same site: the stated accept condition \"SIGABRT, or the message\" admits ANY abort, including an unrelated panic elsewhere in the runtime; only the panic message is specific enough to prove the claims protocol detected the misuse. The fix is a harness in check.sh, in the shape of the stderr-smoke block: run the binary, require a non-zero status AND grep the output for \"CompletionQueue: selected from two tasks\"."}, {"file": "examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig", "line": 78, "severity": "minor", "category": "stability", "title": "The socketpair descriptors now leak if the first feed_mu.lock() fails", "body": "Before this change, `defer _ = std.c.close(fds[0]); defer _ = std.c.close(fds[1]);` were registered immediately after the `fcntl` loop, so every error return past the successful `socketpair` closed both descriptors. The diff moves the closes into a single `defer` block that is registered at line 85, AFTER the `try sh.feed_mu.lock()` at line 78. `Mutex.lock` is cancelable and returns `Cancelable!void` (src/sync/Mutex.zig:71). If the driver task is cancelled while parked on that lock, the `try` propagates `error.Canceled` out of `driver` with the close defer never registered, and both descriptors of that generation leak. The window is narrow and the process is short-lived, so the practical damage is small, but it is a teardown gap introduced by a change whose stated purpose is descriptor-lifetime safety. Register the close defer immediately after the `fcntl` loop (it does not touch `sh.feed_fd`, so it can stay separate from the mutex-guarded clear), or acquire the lock before creating the socketpair."}, {"file": "build.zig", "line": 98, "severity": "minor", "category": "portability", "title": "The posix_only gate keys on Windows only, so the same compile break returns on other non-POSIX targets", "body": "The field is named `posix_only` and its doc comment says the example \"uses POSIX-only APIs (socketpair, fcntl)\", but the guard tests `target.result.os.tag == .windows`. `examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig` reaches `std.c.socketpair`, `std.c.fcntl`, `std.c.F.GETFL` and `std.c.O.NONBLOCK`, none of which exist for wasi or other libc-less non-POSIX targets. Building examples for such a target reproduces exactly the compile failure this change exists to remove, and the field's own documentation then contradicts the behaviour. Gate on the POSIX-ness of the target instead of on a single OS tag, or narrow the field name and its comment to say \"does not build for Windows\"."}]}
